title: Winning the Battle of Life (Kurukshetra Within Me) - Part - 3 | Swami Smaranananda Giri

# Winning the Battle of Life (Kurukshetra Within Me) - Part 3

### The Internal Battlefield

In our ongoing exploration of the Kurukshetra within, we must recognize that the Bhagavad Gita is not merely an ancient historical record. It is a psychological and spiritual map of our own inner lives. The Kurukshetra of the Gita is the Kurukshetra of the human heart, where the ego and its desires are constantly warring against the divine tendencies represented by the Pandavas. 

As Paramahansa Yogananda emphasized, the battle is fought between our lower nature—the restless senses, the attachment to material things, and the ego—and our higher nature, the soul’s intuitive yearning for God.

### The Necessity of Detachment

To win the battle of life, we must learn the art of non-attachment. This does not mean running away from the world. It means acting in the world without being of it. It means fulfilling our duties with a spirit of offering, placing the results of all our actions at the lotus feet of the Divine.

**Story • The King and the Sacred Thread**

Story: There was once a king who sought the highest spiritual truth. He approached a great master and asked how he could remain spiritual while managing a kingdom. The master gave him a bowl filled to the brim with oil and told him to walk around the city without spilling a single drop. If he spilled even a drop, the guards would behead him. The king walked, his focus intense, his mind entirely on the bowl. Upon returning, the master asked him, 'What did you see in the city? Did you see the beautiful gardens, the market, the people?' The king replied, 'Master, my entire focus was on the oil. I saw nothing else.' The master then said, 'That is how you must live. Keep your mind fixed on the inner Divine, and you may walk through the world, perform your duties, and manage your kingdom without letting the world spill out of your consciousness.'

### Meditation as the Weapon

How do we sustain this focus? Through the scientific technique of Kriya Yoga as given by our gurus. Meditation is not just a form of relaxation; it is a sharpening of the sword of discrimination (Viveka). When the mind is quiet, the soul reflects the light of God. When the mind is turbulent, the light is scattered, and we lose our way in the battlefield of life.

We must realize that the Kauravas—our evil tendencies like anger, greed, and jealousy—are formidable opponents. But they are mortal. The Pandavas, led by Krishna (the Divine Consciousness within), are immortal. We only lose the battle when we identify with the Kauravas. When we turn to Krishna, the battle is already won.

### Conclusion: Trusting the Divine Charioteer

We must surrender the reins of our chariot to Krishna. In every thought, in every action, ask: 'Is this what the Lord would do?' This practice, over time, transforms the battlefield into a field of dharma. We stop being reactive to the world and start being responsive to the inner light of the soul.
